technical-data.invention-title: THE AUTOMOTIVE SELF-ADJUSTABLE DAMPER WITH A DISSIPATIVE SELF-CORRECTING CHARACTERISTIC
AMORTISSEUR AUTO-AJUSTABLE AVEC CARACTERISTIQUES AUTO-CORRECTRICES DISSIPATIVES

nplcit.text: "MONROE SENSA-TRAC, UN NOUVEAU CONCEPT" REVUE TECHNIQUE AUTOMOBILE,FR,ETAI. BOULOGNE-BILLANCOURT, vol. 49, no. 567, 1 November 1994 (1994-11-01), page 351 XP000472648 ISSN: 0017-307X

abstract.p: An automative self-adjustable damper having a progressive damping characteristic meant to be used with vehicles for damping the swing of the wheels, chassis, carosserie, the drivers and passengers seats, the engine set as well as in parachoke bars for impact energy absorbtion. This shock absorber is made up of several systems: energy dissipation system, rod volume compensation system, the guiding scaling system and the resistance part protecting all these systems.

L'invention concerne un amortisseur automobile auto-ajustable présentant un amortissement progressif, conçu pour une utilisation sur des véhicules motorisés ou non, dans le but d'amortir les mouvements des roues, du châssis, de la carrosserie, des sièges conducteur et passager, et de l'ensemble moteur. Cet amortisseur peut également être utilisé dans les pare-chocs afin d'absorber l'énergie des impacts. Selon la situation, cet amortisseur peut être utilisé à l'état non-pressurisé, avec une faible pression afin d'améliorer les caractéristiques d'amortissement, ou à l'état pressurisé avec une pression élevée afin d'assurer également une force de flottabilité. Pour amortir les mouvements, il est recommandé d'employer des coefficients d'amortissement élevés, présentant l'inconvénient de réduire le confort. Les suspensions actives et semi-actives permettent de modifier les coefficients d'amortissement en fonction des besoins mais sont de construction complexe, onéreuses et consomment beaucoup d'énergie. Selon l'invention, l'absorbeur de choc présente l'avantage d'offrir une large gamme de coefficients d'amortissement en fonction de la position relative du piston dans le cylindre, ainsi qu'une simplicité technologique. Au niveau du rebond et de la compression, les coefficients d'amortissements sont faibles en début de course, moyens en milieu de course et élevés/très élevés en fin de course. Ainsi, une bonne adhérence entre la roue et la route, ainsi que le confort et la protection sont assurés en fin de course. Cet absorbeur de chocs est réalisé à partir de plusieurs systèmes ; système de dissipation d'énergie, et système de compensation du volume de la tige, le système guidant de mise à l'échelle et la partie résistante assurant la protection de tous ces systèmes.

The invention deals with an automotive self-adjustable damper having a progressive damping characteristic meant to be used with vehicles and motor vehicles for damping the swing of the wheels, chassis, carosserie. the drivers and pasengers seats, the engine set as well as in parachoke bars for impact energy absorbtion. Depending on the situation it can be used unpressurized. at a low pressure for improving the damping characteristic or pressurized at a higli pressure for assuring a buoyant force too.

At higli pressures it can be used as a stabilizer for tlie bonnets and dors both for vehicles and motor vehicles and for civil and industrial constructions, furniture and different household articles.

For damping the oscillations it is recommendable to use higli damping coefficients which have the disadvantage of reducing the contort. The active and semiactive suspensions assure the variation of the damping coefficients function of the needs but they are complicated to build, they are expensive and require higli power consumptions.

One knows a relatively simple solution of the Monroe company called Sensa - Trac. assuring small damping coefficients in tl e medium working area of the piston and so. comfort and normal resting coefficients. The solution is applied to the classical hydraulic shock-absorber and consists to of a cupping of tlie inner cylinder in the medyuni area which increases the hidraulic loss and these decreasing damping coefficients both for tlie rebound stroke and for tlie compression one.

The disadvantages of the solution are due to the technological complication when cupping the cylinder as well as due to the fact that the damping coefficient variation is low not assuring tlie protection at die end of tlie stroke.

According to the invention the shock absorber has the advantage of assuring a large range of damping coefficients --unction of the relative piston position in die cylinder as well as a technological simplicity. Both on rebound and compression , the damping coefficients have low values at tlie beginning of the strokes becoming medium at the middle of the stroke and higli and very higli when getting to tl e end of it. Thus a good adherencv wheel-road, contort and protection at tlie end of die stroke are assured.

This shock absorber is made up of several systems: energy dissipation system, rod volume compensation system, tlie guiding sealing system and the resistance part protecting all these systems. The most principal one is die energy dissipation system consisting of a cylinder, closed at ends with blocks containing or no filling valves or mixed ones filling and checking , having sideways checking valves and eventually filling valves, placed optimum between tlie two ends. A piston with or without
checking valves but without filling valves runs inside the cilynder. Due to this structure the moving of the piston is easier at the begimiing of the stroke because the discarge of the working fluid is on several valves. As the piston approaches the end of the stroke the number of the valves implied decreasses, the resistance increasing accordingly. The situation is similar for both strokes: compression and rebound.

The compensation of the volume of the rod carrying out the stroke can be made through compensating rooms placed above the valves or below them, with a pressurized bladder and with external compensating rooms, at atmospheric pressure or pressurized.
According to the invention the shock absorber has the following advantages:
- at the beginning of tlie stroke it assures low damping coefficients allowing the system to reach quickly tlie medium working area permitting tiius a good confort;
- it assures medium damping coefficients in the medium working area that is an optimum compromise between adherencv and comfort;
- after the medium area it provides increased damping coefficients for a good damping of the carosserie oscillations and assuring a good adherency;

- to the end of the stroke it provides higli damping coefficients eliminating the cushoning at the end of stroke protecting thus the carosserie, mechanic, improving the passanger comfort and eliminating tlie noise specific to this regime;

- with the simple versions die piston does not have valves and the valves located on the inner cylinder are reduced to calibrated holes/ slots providing thus a constructive simplicity, robustness and a low price;

- by applying the version with piston with membranes or little pistons die comfort and adherency at small dislevelment are increased and improve the damping along the others sections which, under tiiese circumstances can be tared for stronger adjustments;
- the replacement of die inner cylinder with valves with a porous cylinder with controlled capillarity assures a solution of a great simplicity, robustness, fiability and low price;
- it is better used to achieve semiactive suspensions having practically infinite checking possibilities;
- it allows achieving the shock- absorbers for parashock bumper, reinforced and adjusted according to the new destination;

- pressurized and tared accordingly it can be used as door balancer, damper for 5 th door of break , shock absorber for revolving doors on vertical axes, for die suspension of the engines or of the driver and passenger seats;
- die lamination of the working fluid through several valves increases die fiability , reduces the noise level and assures a low thermal regime;

The automotive self-adjustable damper with a disipalive self-correcting characteristic according to the first accomplishing example represents die principle design of the invention. A rod (!) drives off a piston (2) in an inner cylinder (3), closed at its inferior end by an mferior block (4) and at its superior end by a superior block (5) containing the rod guiding (6) too. In order to maintain die running liquid above die valves in a dinamic regime, a labyrinth system (7) is atached on superior part. All these elements are introduced in an outer cylinder (8) closed with a lid (9), the rod (!) passes dnough, sealed by a sealmg element Q0). The lid (9) is sealed as to die outer cylinder (8) through a sealing fitting (11). The fixing of the assembly made up by die inner cylinder (3), die lid (9), the mferior (4) and superior (5) blocks and labyrinth (7) is done axially between a proeminence (a) and a cupping (b) of the outer cylmder (8), and die lateral centring is assured by die same proeminence (a) and by a collar (c) of the superior block (5). The inferior block (4) contains an adjusdnent compression valve (12) and a filling rebound (L3) one .
The superior block (5) contains a checking rebound valve Q4) and a filling compression valve ( L5). The piston (2) may contain or not a checking compression valve (16) and/or checking rebound valve (17). The inner cylinder (3) contains checking rebound valves (18) and checking compression valves (1_9) and may contain or not filling rebound valves (20) and filling compression valves (2Λ) placed conveniently as position and number. The checking valves placed on the inner cylinder above die piston always work at the rebound stroke, and the check valves placed under the piston work on compression stroke, so that function of die position and the sense of the piston stroke, the same valve may have a check role on rebound or compression , that is one or several valves (18) may become 09) and die other way round. In the same way, the filling valves placed on the inner cylinder become active on rebound or compression, function of position and the sense of the piston running, thus one or several valves (20) becoming (21) or the other way round. The volume of the rod is compensated through the compensating chamber (d), placed above the valves, the circulation of the liquid between this and enclosure (e) between inner cylinder (3) and outer cylinder (8) and (f) between lower part of the outer cylinder (8) and inferior block (4), being accomplished through some passing holes (g) placed in die superior block (5), in the inner nose (h) respectively, of die outer cylinder (8) and (i) in labyrinths (7).

During the compression stroke due to the superpressure built up under the piston (2), the filling rebound valves (20) in the inner cylinder (3) placed under the piston (2) and filling rebound valve (13) in the inferior block (4) close , die liquid having to pass through the checking compression valves 09) placed on the inner cylinder (3) under die piston (2) and when existing tlirough die checking compression valve (12) in the inferior block (4) and (!6) in piston (2). The more the piston approaches the inferior block (4) die more die number of the active checking compression valves (19) placed in the inner cylinder (3) is reduced and thus the damping force increases due to the increase of die speed of the liquid flowing through these valves. At the same time with the closing of the filling valves from under the piston (2), die filling compression valves (21) placed on die inner cylinder (3) above the piston (2) and/or the filling compression valve (15) in the superior block (5) open due to die pressure differences, assuring die filling witii liquid of the working inside (j) above die piston preparing dius the rebound stroke. The dissipation characteristic function of the position of die piston changes as necessary by the corresponding placing and taring of the checking valves.

At the rebound stroke die overpressure built up above the piston (2) closes die filling compression valves (21 placed in the imier cylinder (3) and/or filling compression valve (15) placed in the superior block (5), forcing the liquid to pass tlirough the checking rebound valves (18) in the inner (3) cylinder, placed above die piston (2) and if any through die checking rebound valve (14) in die superior block
(5) and (17) from piston (2). As the piston approaches the superior block (5), the number of the checking rebound valves (J-8) active decreases so tiiat the damping force increases. The depression from under the piston (2) opens the filling rebound valves (20) from under the piston placed on the inner (3) cylinder and die filling rebound valve ( 13) in the inferior block (4), allowing the filling with liquid of the working area (k) on reboiuid stroke, preparing thus die compression stroke. Function of the location, the number and taring of the checking valves one obtains the required dissipation function as reported to the piston position.

The filling valves can vary in number function of the accomplished version being reduced to two pieces, one in the superior area ( for preparing die rebound stroke) and one in the inferior area ( for preparing the compression stroke ), placed in the blocks or on die inner cylinder. These valves can be wid plates, with segment or with ball. The checking 02) and (14) valves in the inferior block, superior respectively may be missing, so may the checking valves (16) and (17) in the piston. The number of the checking valves in the inner cylinder may be unlimited.

For the correct working of this version one must permanently assure a minimum level of liquid superior to the highest filling valve, thus the valves must be permanently flooded. The requirement is assured by the superior compensating chamber (d), edowed with the labyrints (7) system, for keeping the oil above the valves, in a dynamic regime.
For a better working one may produce a low press urization, for an upward force high pressurization and in the case of using as a balancing unit a high pressurization.
